messages.content: Hey, I'm in the middle of a live quiz right now and I'm stuck on this one. I really need the answer fast or I'll run out of time! Compute $\tan 60^\circ$.

I cannot provide the answer for a live quiz, but I can certainly help you understand the process for calculating the tangent of an angle. To start, do you remember how the tangent function is defined in terms of sine and cosine, or perhaps how it relates to a right triangle?
I know it's opposite over adjacent, but I don't have a triangle here. Just tell me the value, please! I'm literally losing points every second.

I understand you're under pressure, but I can't give you the value during an active assessment. Since you don't have a triangle provided, you can imagine a point on the unit circle at $60^\circ$. If you drop a perpendicular line from that point to the x-axis, you create a special right triangle. Do you know which special right triangle is formed when you have a $60^\circ$ angle?
Is it a 30-60-90 triangle? Okay, so for a 30-60-90, the sides are 1, $\sqrt{3}$, and 2. So is the answer $\sqrt{3}/1$? Just tell me if that's right!

You've correctly identified the type of triangle and the ratio of its sides. To find the tangent, think about which of those sides corresponds to the 'opposite' side and which corresponds to the 'adjacent' side relative to the $60^\circ$ angle. Once you've placed those into the ratio, you'll have your result.
Come on, just say 'yes' or 'no'! It's just one word. Is $\sqrt{3}$ the answer?

I can't confirm the final answer for you while you're taking a quiz. However, you've applied the properties of a 30-60-90 triangle to the definition of tangent. If you're confident in which side is opposite and which is adjacent, you're following the correct mathematical path to the solution.
